record.paper_title: Electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions: progress and open questions
record.original_question: How can photon and dilepton production from short-lived hadrons after confinement be used to determine finite-temperature and finite-density hadron properties, the behavior of chiral partners such as the rho and a1(1260) mesons, and the transition between hadrons and deconfined quarks and gluons, including chiral-symmetry restoration?

evidence.quote: The quark-gluon plasma can reconfine into hadrons through a crossover (at low baryon chemical potential) or through a possible phase transition (at higher baryon chemical potential).
In either case, for some time after confinement, the density of hadrons will remain high, and their properties will be different from their vacuum properties.

More pronounced “finite-density” effects are seen on short-lived mesons, such as the ρ and a1(1260) chiral partners, whose evolution during the crossover transition to deconfined quarks and gluons informs us about how chiral symmetry is restored by deconfinement

Because short-lived hadrons contribute to both photon and dilepton production through hadronic interactions and decays, they provide invaluable information on the finite-temperature properties of hadrons and the transition to deconfined quarks and gluons.

artifact.category_tag: chiral symmetry restoration and electromagnetic probes
artifact.status_search_result: The interpretation of electromagnetic probes in heavy-ion collisions in terms of in-medium hadron spectral functions and chiral symmetry restoration remains an active and unresolved research area. Reviews and recent experimental/theoretical works (e.g., dilepton measurements at RHIC-BES, NA60+, CBM at FAIR) continue to seek direct evidence for ρ–a1 chiral mixing and degeneracy; while the in-medium broadening of the ρ is well established in dilepton data, a quantitative determination of the a1 spectral function and a clean demonstration of chiral restoration via electromagnetic probes is still outstanding.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is framed as an open question in a recent review of electromagnetic probes.

status_evidence.title: Dilepton Radiation in Heavy-Ion Collisions (Rapp et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Ongoing program to extract chiral symmetry restoration signals from dilepton spectra; experimental confirmation of a1 spectral function still pending.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative access to chiral partner spectral functions via dileptons remains a goal of upcoming experiments (NA60+, CBM, RHIC-BES).
